sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Greenspan, in for Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·格林斯潘，代班罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: By now, the story is well known.
sentences.zh: 时至今日，这个故事已广为人知。

sentences.en: A man sits in the backseat of a cab,
sentences.zh: 一个男人坐在出租车后座，

sentences.en: sketching on a notepad as night falls over a crumbling city.
sentences.zh: 在夜幕降临于这座摇摇欲坠的城市时，他在记事本上涂鸦。

sentences.en: He scribbles a letter I.
sentences.zh: 他写下了一个字母“I”。

sentences.en: He draws a heart, and then an N, and then a Y.
sentences.zh: 他画了一颗心，接着是一个“N”，然后是一个“Y”。

sentences.en: And right away, he knows he's got something.
sentences.zh: 他立刻意识到自己有了个好点子。

sentences.en: This is it, he thinks.
sentences.zh: 就是这个，他想。

sentences.en: This is the campaign.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个宣传活动。

sentences.en: The man was a designer named Milton Glaser.
sentences.zh: 这个男人是一位名叫米尔顿·格拉泽的设计师。

sentences.en: The city was New York, the year 1977.
sentences.zh: 这座城市是纽约，时间是1977年。

sentences.en: A time and place commemorated by an entire genre of movies
sentences.zh: 那是一个被整整一个电影流派所铭记的时空，

sentences.en: dedicated to making it look like a terrifying place to live.
sentences.zh: 那些电影致力于将纽约描绘成一个恐怖的居住地。

sentences.en: Enjoy a typical afternoon in New York City, the most violent town in the world.
sentences.zh: 享受在纽约市的典型午后吧，这是世界上最暴力的城镇。

sentences.en: Let's see the money, man.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看钱，伙计。

sentences.en: Can you dig it?
sentences.zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

sentences.en: The city needed a miracle, and it kind of got one, in three letters and a symbol.
sentences.zh: 这座城市需要一个奇迹，而它确实得到了一个，由三个字母和一个符号组成。

sentences.en: I.
sentences.zh: I。

sentences.en: Heart.
sentences.zh: 心。

sentences.en: N.
sentences.zh: N。

sentences.en: Y.
sentences.zh: Y。

sentences.en: Telling the story with me is reporter Muj Zade.
sentences.zh: 和我一起讲述这个故事的是记者穆杰·扎德。

sentences.en: Milton Glaser created the design pro bono for the Empire State Development Corporation.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿·格拉泽为帝国州发展公司免费创作了这个设计。

sentences.en: That's the agency that handles tourism for the state of New York.
sentences.zh: 那是负责纽约州旅游业的机构。

sentences.en: So the N.
sentences.zh: 所以这个“N”。

sentences.en: Y.
actually refers to all of New York State, not just the city.
sentences.zh: 实际上指的是整个纽约州，而不仅仅是纽约市。

sentences.en: So, I used to live in New York, and this logo is literally everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我以前住在纽约，这个标志简直无处不在。

sentences.en: T-shirts, hats, towels, plastic bags, oven mitts.
sentences.zh: T恤、帽子、毛巾、塑料袋、烤箱手套。

sentences.en: For a long time, I didn't even realize that anyone had designed it.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我甚至没意识到这是有人专门设计的。

sentences.en: I didn't like it or dislike it.
sentences.zh: 我谈不上喜欢或讨厌它。

sentences.en: It was just part of New York.
sentences.zh: 它只是纽约的一部分。

sentences.en: Of all the pronoun-verb-noun combinations that have ever been turned into a piece of visual design,
sentences.zh: 在所有被转化为视觉设计的“代词-动词-名词”组合中，

sentences.en: I Love New York is a pretty good one.
sentences.zh: “我爱纽约”算是一个相当不错的作品。

sentences.en: I'll guess that there's not a single person out there in listener land who needs a description.
sentences.zh: 我猜听众里应该没人需要我来描述它。

sentences.en: I do not have to tell you that we are talking about a two-by-two grid, the letters in a typeface with a friendly serif conjoined by a plump red heart.
sentences.zh: 我无需多言，你们都知道那是一个二乘二的网格，字母采用友好的衬线字体，中间连着一颗饱满的红心。

sentences.en: Both New York City and state have their own official flag, but the heart logo may as well be it.
sentences.zh: 纽约市和纽约州都有各自的官方旗帜，但这个心形标志几乎可以取而代之。

sentences.en: And like any good flag, the logo can inspire a sense of civic pride.
sentences.zh: 就像任何优秀的旗帜一样，这个标志能激发一种公民自豪感。

sentences.en: I remember the first time I bought an I Heart New York shirt was actually a couple days after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 我记得我第一次买“我爱纽约”T恤，其实是在9·11事件发生几天后。

sentences.en: I was living in Brooklyn, and I was on my way to work and saw the towers, you know, exploding.
sentences.zh: 当时我住在布鲁克林，在去上班的路上，我看到双子塔，你知道的，爆炸了。

sentences.en: And after that experience, your first thought is, how can I show this city that I love it?
sentences.zh: 在那次经历之后，你脑海中闪过的第一个念头就是：我该如何向这座城市表达我的爱？

sentences.en: And of course, the first thing that comes to your mind is this beautiful piece of art that says I Heart New York.
sentences.zh: 当然，你首先想到的就是这件写着“我爱纽约”的精美艺术品。

sentences.en: And so I went down to Chinatown, and I bought a shirt.
sentences.zh: 于是我去了唐人街，买了一件T恤。

sentences.en: And I'm pretty sure it was probably not an officially licensed product, but it was $5.
sentences.zh: 我很确定它大概不是官方授权产品，但只要5美元。

sentences.en: And I put it on, and I wore it until it smelled bad, and it helped me feel better.
sentences.zh: 我穿上它，一直穿到它发臭，它确实让我感觉好受了一些。

sentences.en: The thing about the I Love NY campaign is that it was so successful that it became part of the built environment.
sentences.zh: “我爱纽约”宣传活动的成功之处在于，它已经成为了建筑环境的一部分。

sentences.en: So people started doing with I Love NY the same thing that humans have always done,
sentences.zh: 所以人们开始对“我爱纽约”做人类一直以来都会做的事情，

sentences.en: when encountering something in nature.
sentences.zh: 当遇到自然界的事物时，

sentences.en: They started imitating it.
sentences.zh: 他们开始模仿它。

sentences.en: My name is Wendy Bryan, and I make plush internal organs for my company, I Heart Guts.
sentences.zh: 我叫温迪·布莱恩，我为我的公司“我爱内脏”制作毛绒内脏器官。

sentences.en: Wendy runs I Heart Guts out of her home in Tacoma Park, Maryland.
sentences.zh: 温迪在马里兰州塔科马公园的家中经营着“我爱内脏”。

sentences.en: She makes these anatomically correct plush dolls of internal organs.
sentences.zh: 她制作这些解剖学上准确的内脏器官毛绒玩偶。

sentences.en: Kidneys, spleens, prostates, uteri, all with faces full of joy.
sentences.zh: 肾脏、脾脏、前列腺、子宫，全都带着充满喜悦的表情。

sentences.en: Wendy started I Heart Guts back in 2005 as a t-shirt business.
sentences.zh: 温迪在2005年创办了“我爱内脏”，最初是一家T恤公司。

sentences.en: The dolls didn't come until later.
sentences.zh: 玩偶是后来才有的。

sentences.en: And one shirt was in the style of I Love NY.
sentences.zh: 其中一件T恤的风格就是模仿“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: Which Wendy knew was not totally groundbreaking material.
sentences.zh: 温迪知道这并不是什么开创性的素材。

sentences.en: You see I Orange New York on the Tropicana ads.
sentences.zh: 你在纯果乐的广告里能看到“我橙纽约”。

sentences.en: You see t-shirts that say I Stomach LA, or I Spade My Cat.
sentences.zh: 你也能看到写着“我胃洛杉矶”或“我绝育我的猫”的T恤。

sentences.en: Spade like clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades.
sentences.zh: 黑桃，就像扑克牌里的梅花、方块、红心、黑桃。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: You see, you know, ripoffs of this iconic graphic design absolutely everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你看，你知道的，这种标志性平面设计的山寨品简直无处不在。

sentences.en: Now Wendy is a huge fan of Milton Glaser.
sentences.zh: 温迪本人是米尔顿·格拉泽的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Remember, he's the guy who created I Love New York.
sentences.zh: 记住，他就是创作了“我爱纽约”的那个人。

sentences.en: He's a genius.
sentences.zh: 他是个天才。

sentences.en: He's a brilliant graphic designer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位杰出的平面设计师。

sentences.en: You go on Etsy, there's about a billion different I Heart New York ripoffs.
sentences.zh: 你去Etsy上看看，大约有十亿种不同的“我爱纽约”山寨品。

sentences.en: And nobody ever says that Milton Glaser is the one who designed this.
sentences.zh: 而且从来没人提过米尔顿·格拉泽是这个标志的设计者。

sentences.en: So I wanted to give the man credit where credit is due.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能给这位大师应得的赞誉。

sentences.en: So, on her website, she put up a note right next to the t-shirt that called it a, quote,
sentences.zh: 于是，她在网站上T恤旁边加了一段说明，称其为，引用：

sentences.en: Fun new tee based on Milton Glaser's iconic I Heart NY design.
sentences.zh: “基于米尔顿·格拉泽标志性‘我爱纽约’设计的趣味新款T恤”。

sentences.en: A few months later, actually on my birthday in July 8th, 2008.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，确切地说是2008年7月8日，我的生日那天。

sentences.en: Your birthday.
sentences.zh: 你的生日？

sentences.en: It was my birthday.
sentences.zh: 那是我的生日。

sentences.en: I got a cease and desist letter that said that I was infringing on the I Heart New York trademark
sentences.zh: 我收到了一封停止侵权信，说我的设计侵犯了“我爱纽约”的商标权，

sentences.en: with my design and could I please destroy all the shirts and take them down from the website.
sentences.zh: 并要求我销毁所有T恤，并将其从网站上撤下。

sentences.en: So I was completely freaked out.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全吓坏了。

sentences.en: I Heart New York, or really I Love New York, is intellectual property owned by New York State.
sentences.zh: “我爱纽约”实际上是纽约州拥有的知识产权。

sentences.en: You can't just riff on it with your own design and sell it without paying for it.
sentences.zh: 你不能随随便便拿它进行二次创作并出售，而不支付费用。

sentences.en: Wendy made some alterations to the merchandise in question,
sentences.zh: 温迪对相关的商品做了一些改动，

sentences.en: like cutting the design out of the shirt and sewing it back onto another shirt upside down and off center.
sentences.zh: 比如把设计从T恤上剪下来，然后倒过来、偏离中心地缝到另一件T恤上。

sentences.en: The difference between an I Heart Guts shirt and an I Orange New York Tropicana ad
sentences.zh: “我爱内脏”T恤和纯果乐的“我橙纽约”广告之间的区别在于，

sentences.en: is that Tropicana paid for the rights to use it.
sentences.zh: 纯果乐支付了使用权费用。

sentences.en: Most likely.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: It's hard to get details on specific legal agreements, but for the most part.
sentences.zh: 很难获得具体法律协议的细节，但大体上是这样。

sentences.en: If you don't pay and you get caught, you get a cease and desist letter.
sentences.zh: 如果你不付钱却被抓住了，你就会收到一封停止侵权信。

sentences.en: Ignore it, and you've got a lawsuit on your hands.
sentences.zh: 无视它，你就会面临诉讼。

sentences.en: Though as far as cease and desist letters go, Wendy said this one was...
sentences.zh: 不过就停止侵权信而言，温迪说这一封……

sentences.en: Really sweet.
sentences.zh: 真的很甜美。

sentences.en: I'm looking at this, you know, scary cease and desist letter
sentences.zh: 我看着这封，你知道的，可怕的停止侵权信，

sentences.en: and have all these, like, sweet little hearts all over it just scattered all over the page.
sentences.zh: 上面却散布着各种甜美的小心心，到处都是。

sentences.en: Ironically, it may have been the shout-out to Milton Glaser that got Wendy in trouble.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，可能正是因为提到了米尔顿·格拉泽才让温迪惹上了麻烦。

sentences.en: Or at least she thinks so.
sentences.zh: 或者至少她是这么认为的。

sentences.en: There's really no way to tell.
sentences.zh: 真的没法确定。

sentences.en: I figured that they probably have legal spider robots that are constantly searching for search terms,
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能有一些法律蜘蛛机器人，一直在搜索关键词，

sentences.en: like Milton Glaser, or I Heart New York, or I Love New York.
sentences.zh: 比如“米尔顿·格拉泽”、“我爱纽约”或“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: We do Google searches, and we receive Google alerts.
sentences.zh: 我们做谷歌搜索，也会收到谷歌快讯。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think any of this information is very groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不觉得这些信息有什么开创性。

sentences.en: That's Claire Newman.
sentences.zh: 那是克莱尔·纽曼。

sentences.en: My name is Claire Newman, and I am an IP Licensing Executive and Legal Counsel for CMG Worldwide,
sentences.zh: 我叫克莱尔·纽曼，我是CMG全球公司的知识产权许可主管兼法律顾问，

sentences.en: and we represent the New York State Department of Economic Development,
sentences.zh: 我们代表纽约州经济发展部，

sentences.en: who is the proprietor and owner of the I Heart NY trademark.
sentences.zh: 他们是“我爱纽约”商标的所有者和拥有者。

sentences.en: So it's I Heart, not I Love?
sentences.zh: 所以是“我心”，而不是“我爱”？

sentences.en: It is actually I Love.
sentences.zh: 实际上是“我爱”。

sentences.en: I can't believe I messed that up.
sentences.zh: 真不敢相信我搞错了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's I Love New York.
sentences.zh: 是的，是“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: CMG handles intellectual property licensing for, according to their website,
sentences.zh: 根据他们的网站，CMG负责处理知识产权许可，

sentences.en: celebratory individuals from then, now, and forever.
sentences.zh: 对象是过去、现在和未来的名人。

sentences.en: They represent the estates of Amelia Earhart, Malcolm X, Frank Lloyd Wright, and a bunch of other famous dead people.
sentences.zh: 他们代表阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特、马尔科姆·X、弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特以及其他许多已故名人的遗产。

sentences.en: And of course, I Love New York, which Claire Newman represents from her office in Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有克莱尔·纽曼在印第安纳波利斯办公室所代表的“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: Claire says about half of her workload is related to licensing I Love New York.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔说她大约一半的工作量都与“我爱纽约”的授权有关。

sentences.en: And she has a number of colleagues who work on it, too.
sentences.zh: 她也有许多同事在做这项工作。

sentences.en: Though, to be clear, it wasn't Claire who sent Wendy the cease and desist letter.
sentences.zh: 不过要说明的是，给温迪发停止侵权信的并不是克莱尔。

sentences.en: That happened before Claire was working with CMG.
sentences.zh: 那是在克莱尔加入CMG之前发生的。

sentences.en: Her office works with interested vendors, like t-shirt manufacturers, to license the logo as is.
sentences.zh: 她的办公室与感兴趣的供应商（如T恤制造商）合作，对标志进行原样授权。

sentences.en: Or a company can pay to remix the logo, like Tropicana did, with I, Orange, and Y.
sentences.zh: 或者公司也可以付费对标志进行重新设计，就像纯果乐那样，用“我”、“橙”和“Y”。

sentences.en: Claire looks for infringements on sites like Etsy, Polyvore, and PintereSt.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔会在Etsy、Polyvore和Pinterest等网站上寻找侵权行为。

sentences.en: She says people even report infringements to CMG, and sometimes she just stumbles into them.
sentences.zh: 她说人们甚至会向CMG举报侵权行为，有时她只是偶然发现。

sentences.en: Like today, for example, we got a mailing from a cruise line, and there was an infringement inside the letter.
sentences.zh: 比如今天，我们收到了一家邮轮公司的邮件，信里就包含了一处侵权。

sentences.en: So it was really coincidental, but, you know, we found it.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很巧，但你知道，我们发现了它。

sentences.en: Claire says they have some other methods for searching for infringements that she couldn't talk about.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔说他们还有其他一些搜索侵权的方法，她不便透露。

sentences.en: Her job at CMG is about protecting artists, and Claire says that intellectual property is about protecting consumers, too.
sentences.zh: 她在CMG的工作是保护艺术家，克莱尔说知识产权也是为了保护消费者。

sentences.en: You know, if you buy McDonald's french fries, you know you're getting McDonald's french fries.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你买麦当劳的薯条，你知道你买到的是麦当劳的薯条。

sentences.en: You're not getting Burger King's french fries.
sentences.zh: 你买到的不是汉堡王的薯条。

sentences.en: And so if you started putting different french fries in the McDonald's containers, that trademark...
sentences.zh: 所以如果你开始在麦当劳的包装盒里放不同的薯条，那个商标……

sentences.en: That is the trademark on the container.
sentences.zh: 那就是包装盒上的商标。

sentences.en: ...would stop indicating the source and origin of those french fries.
sentences.zh: ……将不再能指示那些薯条的来源和产地。

sentences.en: So, you know, the reason people use trademarks is so that they can go back to trusted brands and trusted labels,
sentences.zh: 所以，人们使用商标的原因是他们可以回到值得信赖的品牌和标签，

sentences.en: and they know they're getting the same standard and the same type of product each time.
sentences.zh: 他们知道每次都能获得相同标准和相同类型的产品。

sentences.en: But if CMG is saying that an iHeartGuts t-shirt is too close to the Glazer design, I got to wondering, how close is too close?
sentences.zh: 但如果CMG说“我爱内脏”T恤太接近格拉泽的设计，我开始好奇，多近才算太近？

sentences.en: I want to play a game.
sentences.zh: 我想玩个游戏。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Basically, I'm just going to give you potential logos that I came up with.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我会给你看一些我想出来的潜在标志。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Like, whether or not I would think that they would be an infringement?
sentences.zh: 比如，我是否认为它们会构成侵权？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's say you saw I Stomach New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 假设你看到了“我胃新泽西”。

sentences.en: Stomach?
sentences.zh: 胃？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess I would say yes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我会说是的。

sentences.en: I Bike Melbourne.
sentences.zh: “我骑行墨尔本”。

sentences.en: I, and then a bicycle, and then Melbourne.
sentences.zh: “我”，然后是一辆自行车，然后是“墨尔本”。

sentences.en: I mean, I...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我……

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想是吧。

sentences.en: I would have to see it.
sentences.zh: 我得亲眼看看。

sentences.en: It's all about, like, the design and, like, what the visual is invoking.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于设计以及视觉效果所引发的联想。

sentences.en: CMG is vigilant about trademark protection because they have to be.
sentences.zh: CMG在商标保护方面非常警惕，因为他们必须这样做。

sentences.en: The way the law works is that if you don't defend your trademark well enough, you can lose it.
sentences.zh: 法律的运作方式是，如果你不能充分保护你的商标，你可能会失去它。

sentences.en: Say you think someone is ripping off work that you've trademarked, and you try to sue them.
sentences.zh: 假设你认为有人在剽窃你注册了商标的作品，于是你试图起诉他们。

sentences.en: If they can prove that you've done a bad job enforcing that trademark in the past, a judge can wind up siding with them.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能证明你过去在维护该商标方面做得不够好，法官最终可能会站在他们那边。

sentences.en: So it's CMG's job to err on the side of thinking that something is an infringement.
sentences.zh: 所以CMG的工作就是宁可错杀，也要认为某些东西构成了侵权。

sentences.en: My position is that everything is an infringement.
sentences.zh: 我的立场是，一切都是侵权。

sentences.en: Wait, why?
sentences.zh: 等等，为什么？

sentences.en: Because it's my job to protect the mark.
sentences.zh: 因为保护这个商标是我的工作。

sentences.en: Though just because Claire thinks something is an infringement, it doesn't always mean there's a cease and desist letter in the mail from CMG.
sentences.zh: 虽然克莱尔认为某事构成侵权，并不总是意味着CMG会寄出停止侵权通知函。

sentences.en: They send out about 200 I Love NY-related cease and desists per year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年大约会发出200份与“我爱纽约”相关的停止侵权通知函。

sentences.en: Ironically, one of the people to receive such a letter was Milton Glaser, who, remember, did the original I Love NY design for free in 2001, right after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，收到此类信件的人之一竟然是米尔顿·格拉泽，别忘了，他在2001年9·11事件后，免费创作了最初的“我爱纽约”设计。

sentences.en: In an effort to raise money for local New York charities.
sentences.zh: 为了给纽约当地的慈善机构筹集资金。

sentences.en: Glaser created a new modified design that read, I Love NY more than ever.
sentences.zh: 格拉泽创作了一个新的修改版设计，上面写着“我比以往任何时候都更爱纽约”。

sentences.en: The state of New York wound up apologizing to Glaser and chalked it up to a bureaucratic misunderstanding.
sentences.zh: 纽约州最终向格拉泽道歉，并将此事归咎于官僚主义的误解。

sentences.en: Now, we can go back and forth about whether or not this indicates that something is broken in trademark law.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可以反复讨论这是否表明商标法存在缺陷。

sentences.en: But really, the more interesting question is, why does CMG need a whole team of people working on I Love NY?
sentences.zh: 但真正更有趣的问题是，为什么CMG需要一整个团队来处理“我爱纽约”的相关事宜？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: who would have thought that a government ad campaign from the 70s would need to be defended by a team of lawyers from getting stolen and remixed and modified into countless permutations?
sentences.zh: 谁会想到一个70年代的政府广告活动，竟然需要一队律师来保护，防止它被窃取、混剪和修改成无数种变体？

sentences.en: I don't get it.
sentences.zh: 我不明白。

sentences.en: I just, I totally don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我完全无法理解。

sentences.en: And I have done a lot of things that are persistent in the culture.
sentences.zh: 我做过很多在文化中具有持久影响的事情。

sentences.en: You know, stuff that lasts five years, six years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些能持续五六年之久的东西。

sentences.en: Nothing like this.
sentences.zh: 但没有像这样的。

sentences.en: It doesn't make any sense at all.
sentences.zh: 这完全说不通。

sentences.en: And you can probably guess who this is.
sentences.zh: 你可能猜到这是谁了。

sentences.en: My name is Milton Glaser.
sentences.zh: 我叫米尔顿·格拉泽。

sentences.en: I'm a designer.
sentences.zh: 我是一名设计师。

sentences.en: And I spend my day pushing things around until they look good.
sentences.zh: 我每天都在摆弄各种东西，直到它们看起来顺眼为止。

sentences.en: That's what I do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的工作。

sentences.en: It was clear from the beginning of our conversation that Milton Glaser is really over talking about I Love NY.
sentences.zh: 从我们谈话的一开始就很明显，米尔顿·格拉泽已经厌倦了谈论“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: He's done a ton of other work.
sentences.zh: 他还有过大量其他作品。

sentences.en: He did an iconic Bob Dylan poster and Philip Roth book covers.
sentences.zh: 他创作了标志性的鲍勃·迪伦海报和菲利普·罗斯的书籍封面。

sentences.en: He co-founded New York Magazine.
sentences.zh: 他是《纽约》杂志的联合创始人。

sentences.en: And at 84 years old, he's still working.
sentences.zh: 84岁高龄的他依然在工作。

sentences.en: Just recently, he designed an entire visual identity for Brooklyn Brewery.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，他为布鲁克林啤酒厂设计了整套视觉识别系统。

sentences.en: Yet for all his expertise as a designer, even he doesn't understand the success of I Love NY.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管他作为设计师拥有丰富的专业知识，连他自己也不理解“我爱纽约”为何如此成功。

sentences.en: I would have thought it would have lost meaning a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我本以为它很久以前就会失去意义了。

sentences.en: In fact, I thought that it would be a six-month campaign.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我以为那只会是一个为期六个月的活动。

sentences.en: I thought that in 77, it would probably last six months and I'd be done with it.
sentences.zh: 我以为在77年，它大概只会持续六个月，然后我就完成了。

sentences.en: And then when it went through 77 and 78, I thought, well, maybe it has another six months to go.
sentences.zh: 后来它度过了77年和78年，我想，好吧，也许它还能再持续六个月。

sentences.en: And then it went through 78 and 79.
sentences.zh: 然后它又度过了78年和79年。

sentences.en: And here we are after so many decades and it still persists.
sentences.zh: 几十年过去了，我们依然在这里，它依然存在。

sentences.en: I can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I mean, there is no doubt that I will go out into the street today and I will see half a dozen versions of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，毫无疑问，我今天走在街上，肯定会看到它的六七个版本。

sentences.en: If you go down to Chinatown, every building, every street, every side of a wall is covered with I Love NY.
sentences.zh: 如果你去唐人街，每一栋建筑、每一条街道、每一面墙上都贴满了“我爱纽约”。

sentences.en: I mean, there are far more I Love NY than dumplings in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 我是说，唐人街里的“我爱纽约”比饺子多得多。

sentences.en: I mean, why?
sentences.zh: 我是说，为什么？

sentences.en: Why does it persist?
sentences.zh: 它为什么能持续存在？

sentences.en: I thought you'd be able to tell us.
sentences.zh: 我以为你能告诉我们。

sentences.en: No, I wish I could.
sentences.zh: 不，我希望我能。

sentences.en: Why isn't it tiresome?
sentences.zh: 为什么它不会让人厌倦？

sentences.en: Everything is tiresome.
sentences.zh: 万物皆会让人厌倦。

sentences.en: Maybe I Love NY is still around because people just love New York.
sentences.zh: 也许“我爱纽约”依然存在，是因为人们就是爱纽约。

sentences.en: But Milton Glaser thinks that its success has less to do with what the design represents and more with what it is.
sentences.zh: 但米尔顿·格拉泽认为，它的成功与其设计所代表的意义关系不大，更多是与它本身有关。

sentences.en: You know, I think it really has more to do with the peculiarity of brain function than it does to any kind of logic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这更多是与大脑功能的特殊性有关，而不是任何逻辑。

sentences.en: It has something to do with the rigidity of that letter form and the attempt of the grid to contain the erotic nature of the heart.
sentences.zh: 这与字母形式的刚性，以及网格试图容纳心脏所蕴含的情欲特质有关。

sentences.en: There's something that creates an act of closure in people's minds when they see it that they won't repeat it, that doesn't bore them.
sentences.zh: 当人们看到它时，大脑中会产生一种闭合感，这种感觉让他们不会重复它，也不会感到厌烦。

sentences.en: They can look at it a thousand times, a hundred thousand times, and still not saying, I've had enough.
sentences.zh: 他们可以看上一千次、十万次，却依然不会说“我受够了”。

sentences.en: It's a trivial mystery, but maybe not.
sentences.zh: 这是一个微不足道的谜题，但也可能并非如此。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a profound mystery why people are willing to look at certain things over and over and over and over.
sentences.zh: 也许人们愿意一遍又一遍地观看某些事物，这本身就是一个深刻的谜题。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a show of Piero della Francesca at The Frick this week, and I'm going to try to go up there today.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这周弗里克收藏馆有皮耶罗·德拉·弗朗切斯卡的展览，我打算今天去看看。
zh_words: 皮耶罗·德拉·弗朗切斯卡

sentences.en: I'm thinking of Piero.
sentences.zh: 我在想皮耶罗。

sentences.en: I love Piero.
sentences.zh: 我爱皮耶罗。

sentences.en: Why am I willing to look at the same pair of feet and the way they cling to the ground in a Piero?
sentences.zh: 为什么我愿意盯着皮耶罗画中同一双脚，以及它们紧贴地面的方式看个不停？

sentences.en: No other feet at any other painting can make me pay attention for that long.
sentences.zh: 没有任何其他画作中的脚能让我关注那么久。

sentences.en: For my whole life, I've been looking at that same pair of feet, and I'll be looking at it till the day I die with astonishment.
sentences.zh: 我一生都在注视着那双脚，直到我死的那天，我依然会带着惊叹注视着它。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, maybe beyond the I love New York and the phrase and the meaning to the city, there is simply the mystery of form.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许除了“我爱纽约”这个短语及其对城市的意义之外，还存在着形式的奥秘。

sentences.en: Why does a certain curve and a certain color and a certain contrast hold our attention, and why do certain other forms bore us?
sentences.zh: 为什么某种曲线、某种颜色和某种对比能吸引我们的注意力，而其他形式却让我们感到厌烦？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think the most wonderful thing about all of this stuff, all of graphics and all of language and all of color, is the fact you never get to the reason.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些东西——所有的图形、所有的语言和所有的色彩——最美妙的地方在于，你永远无法找到原因。

sentences.en: Maybe the I love NY design continues to hold our attention because of its infinite capacity for remix, that you can substitute literally any part of the equation, the I, the heart,
sentences.zh: 也许“我爱纽约”的设计之所以能持续吸引我们的注意力，是因为它具有无限的混剪潜力，你可以替换掉这个等式中的任何部分：那个“我”，那个心形，

sentences.en: the NY.
sentences.zh: 那个“纽约”。

sentences.en: And the cultural reference still comes across.
sentences.zh: 而文化指涉依然能够传达出来。

sentences.en: In fact, even New York State is doing this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，连纽约州自己也在这样做。

sentences.en: You can now find official spinoff logos like, I pizza New York, and I beach ball New York.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以找到官方的衍生标志，比如“我披萨纽约”和“我沙滩球纽约”。

sentences.en: It is now easier than ever before in human history to take something and change it just enough to make it your own.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史上，现在比以往任何时候都更容易获取某样东西，并对其进行微调，使之成为你自己的作品。

sentences.en: Imitating and altering and remixing has always been the way that humans engage with the world.
sentences.zh: 模仿、改变和混剪一直是人类与世界互动的方式。

sentences.en: But there's a limit here.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个限度。

sentences.en: There will always be a baseline need for new ideas to break free of what's been done and say something truly original.
sentences.zh: 人们总是需要新的创意来打破常规，说出真正原创的东西。

sentences.en: And should you ever fall short of the mark?
sentences.zh: 如果你没能达到那个标准呢？

sentences.en: Somewhere out there is a cease and desist letter waiting to tell you precisely that.
sentences.zh: 在某个地方，有一封停止侵权通知函正等着告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: Here's a postscript.
sentences.zh: 这里有个附言。

sentences.en: Wendy Bryan from iHeartGuts says that there's a silver lining to getting that cease and desist letter from CMG.
sentences.zh: 来自iHeartGuts的温迪·布莱恩说，收到CMG的停止侵权通知函其实也有好的一面。

sentences.en: The language was obviously very frightening, you know.
sentences.zh: 那措辞显然非常吓人，你知道的。

sentences.en: Will not be tolerated.
sentences.zh: 绝不容忍。

sentences.en: Immediate cease and desiSt.
sentences.zh: 立即停止侵权。

sentences.en: There will be a fee.
sentences.zh: 将会有罚款。

sentences.en: So it was terrifying, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这很可怕，对吧？

sentences.en: But later on, I actually was able to use the language from the cease and desist to send out my own cease and desist to people who are ripping off my stuff.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我实际上能够利用那封停止侵权通知函里的措辞，向那些剽窃我作品的人发送我自己的停止侵权通知函。

sentences.en: I'm not the only person who put a happy face on an organ, and I don't claim to be.
sentences.zh: 我不是唯一一个把笑脸画在器官上的人，我也不声称自己是。

sentences.en: But you have to use different colors and different shapes, and you have to come up with your own idea.
sentences.zh: 但你必须使用不同的颜色和形状，你必须想出你自己的点子。

sentences.en: So again, thanks, Melton.
sentences.zh: 所以再次感谢你，米尔顿。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Mooj Zadie, Roman Mars, and me, Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由穆吉·扎迪、罗曼·马尔斯和我，萨姆·格林斯潘制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio KALW in San Francisco and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7本地公共广播电台KALW和旧金山美国建筑师协会的一个项目。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Debbie Millman for helping this episode come together.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢黛比·米尔曼促成了这一集的制作。

sentences.en: If you like hearing designers talk to other designers about design, then you will love Debbie Millman's Design Matters podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢听设计师们谈论设计，那么你一定会喜欢黛比·米尔曼的《设计至上》播客。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在Twitter、Instagram和Spotify上。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links, and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但要了解更多关于这个故事的信息，包括酷炫的图片和链接，并收听《99%隐形》的所有剧集，你必须访问99pi.org。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
